assumptions: The opportunity is assessed at planning stage with no customers, paid pilots, referral commitments, or proprietary registry access beyond the evidence provided.
The supplier, authorised representative, or importer retains legal responsibility; the service does not test, certify, approve, or guarantee List ZUM placement.
The proposed prices, 55-70% blended gross margin, monitoring retention, customer count, and 6-9 year founder-wealth path remain hypotheses rather than validated economics.
The founder continues full-time employment, limits the business to roughly 10-16 hours weekly, and buys accredited testing and specialist interpretation when needed.
List ZUM remains commercially relevant, but future programme and evidence-rule changes may either create paid update work or reduce the service burden.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots across several independent suppliers showing recurrent correction or launch work, measured hours and first-pass outcomes versus self-service, annual model-family frequency and retention, signed laboratory or distributor referral terms, and cohort unit economics covering CAC, specialist cost, gross margin, payback, and renewal would support a higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A real, model-specific subsidy gate makes identifier and evidence consistency commercially consequential, and the proposed preflight sits at a concrete point immediately before submission or update. The insight is narrower than a proprietary compliance control point because placement is free, suppliers can submit directly, and simpler evidence routes now cover several categories.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Incorrect or incomplete records can delay subsidised Polish sales, and the 2025 EPREL reconciliation demonstrates episodic operational pain. Adjacent paid documentation help gives a plausible basis for outsourcing, but the packet contains no direct customer interviews, paid demand, rejection frequency, price sensitivity, or evidence that accepted suppliers want recurring monitoring; the free official workflow is a meaningful substitute.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A fixed-fee, document-led pilot is capital-light and could support reasonable service gross margins if specialist review is controlled. However, pricing, CAC, LTV, retention, payback, project frequency, and owner earnings are all hypothetical, software-like margins are not yet credible, and the stated path to 100-150 recurring suppliers appears much larger than the evidenced Polish wedge.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Non-Polish heat-pump suppliers and Polish importers launching model families form a specific, reachable use case with a clear paid event. Yet the distinct supplier count and reachable foreign-supplier count are unknown, and the evidence explicitly leaves open whether a Poland-only register can sustain a meaningful standalone business.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The service could specialise in cross-document reconciliation and Polish-language workflow coordination, but it controls neither testing, authorisation, the registry, nor a committed channel. Accredited laboratories, distributors, suppliers, and existing compliance providers are all positioned to perform or absorb the same work, so a dominant beachhead position is not presently supported.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning repeat supplier relationships could create openings into EPREL, adjacent energy-labelling work, other device categories, and other European subsidy registers. That expansion is plausible but unvalidated, and country- and category-specific rules may require new expertise and distribution rather than allowing the Polish workflow to scale directly.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned mappings and exception histories could improve delivery speed, but no evidence shows exclusivity, durable data rights, switching costs, network effects, or protected access. Official records and APIs are available, the workflow is learnable, and laboratories or consultancies can build comparable templates while holding stronger evidence relationships.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A single preflight spanning reports, labels, EPREL, identifiers, and ZUM forms may reduce coordination effort and rework for a foreign supplier. The size of that improvement has not been measured, and the offer is not yet shown to be materially faster, cheaper, safer, or more trusted than direct submission or adjacent compliance services.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Continued invoice-date eligibility and changing product records create an ongoing reason to keep evidence aligned, while recent EPREL clean-up shows that rule transitions can generate concentrated work. Conversely, the documented backlog was deadline-driven and recent simplification reduced the burden for several categories, so current momentum may be episodic rather than compounding.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Laboratories, master distributors, an adjacent EPREL provider, and the family HVAC channel are sensible routes for pilots without camera-led promotion. None has committed to refer or white-label the service, commercial terms are unknown, the family channel is closer to downstream installation than foreign OEM buying, and the proposed partners can internalise the workflow.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A document-only pilot fits the founder's data, automation, capital, time, and family-industry access, and specialist review can be purchased rather than recreated. Execution still depends on supplier authorisation, access to sensitive reports, disciplined liability boundaries, data controls, accurate regulatory interpretation, and external accredited expertise; those requirements are obtainable but operationally material.

highest_value_structural_change: Make an accredited laboratory or master distributor the contracted white-label channel and anchor payer, bundling ZUM preflight with paid multi-register launch and change-event operations; secure minimum volume plus permission to retain anonymised exception patterns so distribution, recurrence, and a proprietary validation corpus improve together.
main_structural_strength: A narrow, consequential pre-submission evidence gate can be tested as a low-capital, part-time managed service using the founder's data-automation strengths and family HVAC access.
primary_score_limiter: The opportunity lacks evidence of repeat willingness to pay and a scalable acquisition route in a potentially small Polish wedge, while suppliers and stronger channel holders can use or internalise the free official workflow.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: List ZUM placement is free and directly available to authorised suppliers, evidence routes have been simplified for several categories, EPREL already supplies workflows and APIs, and an adjacent provider already sells overlapping documentation support.
